name: Albion Affordable Apartments (Rise at University Hills)
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Delwest Development is building Albion Affordable Apartments, now marketed as Rise at University Hills: about 170 two- to four-bedroom family apartments for households at 30% to 70% AMI at South Albion Street and East Iliff Avenue near RTD's Colorado Station, with an on-site early childhood center; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $43.75M of CHFA bonds and is due for completion in summer 2027.
why_it_matters: It is a rare family-sized (no studios or one-bedrooms) tax credit deal in a high-cost, high-opportunity part of southeast Denver, assembled from four commercial parcels with a $6.76M city land acquisition loan and a city all-electric rebate.

status.label: Under construction per the developer (page dated 2026-10-07); completion expected summer 2027
status.detail: Delwest closed on the land in October 2024 and its project page, published 2026-10-07, says the seven-story building is under construction with completion in summer 2027. The city extended the deadline for completing the project to 2027-11-01 in May 2025 and signed a heat pump rebate agreement in December 2025. No financing closing or groundbreaking date was found.

next_step: Watch Denver permit and inspection records for 2280 S. Albion Street and for lease-up notices in 2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 124 two-bedroom, 29 three-bedroom and 16 four-bedroom units: 27 at 30% AMI, 61 at 60% and 81 at 70%.
About $37.7M over 10 years, plus $1,100,000 of state credit.
CHFA is the issuer; the application also planned $29.8M of CHFA permanent loans.
Linkage-fee loan at 1% simple interest, repaid from cash flow over 40 years, with a 99-year affordability covenant.

facts.value: Northeast corner of S. Albion St and E. Iliff Ave, Denver 80222 (CHFA); 2222 to 2280 S. Albion Street (city loan); University Hills neighborhood, Council District 4
Marketed as Rise at University Hills

Five stories of wood frame over a two-story concrete podium with structured parking (seven stories), nine two-story four-bedroom townhomes along Albion Street, a 10,000 sq ft clubhouse and a small commercial space; about 114 units per acre

Licensed space for an early childhood center with Wildflower Schools at a $1-a-year lease, with preference for children eligible for the Colorado Child Care Assistance Program and Universal Preschool; Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Denver programming planned
Albion Apartments LLLP; Albion Apartments LLC is an affiliate controlled through the same sole member
Existing zoning allows the use; plans reviewed under Denver's Affordable Housing Review Team, per the application
Denver Housing Authority property tax abatement anticipated, per the application
About 0.2 miles from RTD's Colorado Station; RTD passes for all residents
Denver rental and occupancy covenant of 99 years from recording

money.note: 2023 Round Two; the application budgeted $33.7M of federal credit equity.
The application budgeted $4.6M of state credit equity.
CHFA is the issuer; the application listed up to $29.21M of construction loans and $29.8M of CHFA permanent loans.

The city's May 2025 loan amendment attaches a subordination form naming Wells Fargo Bank as senior lender on a $58M convertible construction loan dated 2025; the city caps senior debt at $58M construction and $33M permanent.

money.source: City and County of Denver loan (linkage fee)
money.note: For land acquisition; 1% simple interest, cash-flow payments, 40-year maturity; resolution 24-1127 adopted 2024-09-23; note dated 2024-10-07 and deed of trust recorded 2024-10-08; amended by resolution 25-0644 on 2025-05-19 to change transfer, cure and notice terms and set a 2027-11-01 completion date.
Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency pilot rebate for heat pump equipment; resolution 25-1808 adopted 2025-12-22; work to be completed within 36 months.

money.source: Other sources named in the application
money.note: The application sought $7.68M each from Denver and the Colorado Division of Housing and deferred $3.7M (45%) of developer fee; no Division of Housing award was found.

parties.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Denver

background.text: The site assembles four occupied parcels with one-story 1950s-60s commercial buildings (2222, 2236-2250 and 2280 S. Albion Street) from three sellers; a fifth parcel at 4175 E. Iliff Ave was dropped because of its different zoning, per the application.
Delwest closed on the roughly 1.5-acre site in October 2024 for $7.5 million, per BusinessDen.

Albion Apartments LLLP deeded two small corner parcels to the city on 2025-02-13 for South Albion Street and East Iliff Avenue right-of-way; council accepted the dedication on 2025-04-07 (resolution 25-0366). The city's summary says the project demolishes four commercial buildings for a mixed-use apartment building.

The 2023 application described gas-fired central boilers designed for later conversion; by December 2025 the owner had signed a city rebate agreement committing to an all-electric building under the 2022 Denver Energy Code.
The application stressed applying in 2023 because the census tract's Qualified Census Tract status was under review and could be lost.
The market study's capture rates were 6.4% or lower at every income level; other tax credit properties in the market area were 98% occupied with waiting lists of 36 to 300 households.
The application planned construction from April 2025 to about April 2027 and lease-up by the end of 2027; the contractor estimate was about $294,000 per unit and a basis limit waiver was requested.
